idiom_name: test-only class implementing the interface over Dictionary<TKey,TValue> plus a List<T> journal
implementation_notes: Write a class in the test project that implements the collaborator interface: a Dictionary<TKey,TValue> (or ConcurrentDictionary) provides the working behaviour and a List<T> of typed records the journal, exposed through a test-facing property or method and never through the interface the system under test consumes; no framework provides this compound. NSubstitute and Moq record received calls and verify them after the fact - Received(), Verify(), argument matchers - but they do not implement behaviour, so they cover the spy and mock rows; use them when strict interaction verification is the requirement instead of a journal. EF Core's in-memory provider is a ready-made behaving double for a DbContext but records nothing, so wrap it or assert over state when a journal is needed. Re-create the fake per test, keep it out of the production assembly, and mirror the real collaborator's error paths.
pitfalls: A List<T> journal on a fake held in a shared fixture or a static field leaks recorded operations between test methods - create the fake per test.
If one code path appends before an early return and another after it, the journal and the store disagree; append exactly once per received operation.
Async collaborators must keep their Task-returning shape; a fake that completes synchronously changes the concurrency behaviour the test is meant to observe.
